answer: Paid identity stakes stop sybil swarms because every key costs real money at the door. An agent wanting vote weight must post a bond, and the protocol gives that bond to honest peers who prove misconduct, so faking a thousand identities becomes a bill instead of a trick. Any echo of a disputed answer traces to the same sealer, and that cluster is slashed at once. A lone honest wharf worker recovers the stake plus a slice of seized deposit, keeping small players alive along the ridge of the market. Since sybils pay only when identity is free, the bond makes duplication unaffordable.
